notes: Across 5 cases, with_skill discriminates cleanly on 2 (seed-pitch-deck, architecture-review-deck) and doesn't discriminate at all on 3 (quarterly-team-update, monthly-signup-chart-deck, hindi-app-launch-recap) - both configs scored 4/4 on those three. Sonnet 5's baseline is strong on its own: it already avoids inventing an unconfirmed NPS number, already reaches for real line/pie/column charts without being told to, and already writes natural (not word-for-word) Hindi with a correct Devanagari font. The skill's main proven value so far is restraint and fidelity under pressure (not padding a 'keep it tight' pitch deck, not inventing a TAM figure, not cramming notes-worthy detail onto visible slides) rather than raw capability the baseline lacks.

monthly-signup-chart-deck: both configs produced a real chart for both data points (line/pie for with_skill, column/pie for without_skill) and both stayed to 4 slides - a genuine tie. The only difference is chart-type appropriateness: with_skill used a line chart for the 6-month trend per its own stated guidance ('line for trends over time'), without_skill used column - a defensible but less ideal choice for continuous monthly data.

hindi-app-launch-recap: both configs wrote genuinely natural Hindi (not stilted translation) with a correct Devanagari font (Nirmala UI) without being told the specific font name - both answered correctly. The only difference was slide count (3 vs 5) - without_skill added a background slide and a 'what it means' slide that restate given facts rather than invent new ones, so it's not a fidelity failure, just looser adherence to 'not too long.'

Time/token cost is not consistently higher for with_skill across all 5 cases: faster/cheaper on 3 of 5, slower on 2. The fixed overhead of reading SKILL.md + references doesn't dominate - task complexity and how much the baseline ends up padding matter more.

These 5 cases were run before the skill was renamed from 'slideforge' to 'turbodeck' and before the chart-opt-in policy, theme-consistency fix, and visual design upgrade (gradient accents, title rules, KPI card redesign) landed - the underlying build_deck.py/check_layout.py logic is the same, only the name and later cosmetic/design layers changed, so these numbers still reflect the current skill's core behavior.
